label: ThmA
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{ThmA}
Let $k_0$ be an imaginary quadratic field.
Let $p$ be an odd prime that is non-split in $k_0$.
Let $A_0$ (resp.~$A_1$) be the $p$-Sylow subgroup of the class group of $k_0$ (resp.~$k_1$).
Let $c$ denote the dimension of the subspace of $A_1/pA_1$ generated by the images of classes lifted from $A_0$.
Then 
\[
\operatorname{rk}_p A_0 +(p-1)c \le \operatorname{rk}_p A_1  \le p \operatorname{rk}_p A_0.
\]
In particular, at most $\lfloor (\operatorname{rk}_p A_1 - \operatorname{rk}_p A_0)/(p-1)\rfloor$ cyclic factors of $A_0$ fail to grow.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\emph{[Theorem~\ref{thm 4.7}]}
If $\operatorname{rk}_p A_0 = \operatorname{rk}_p A_1=r_0$, then $A_1 \cong \bigoplus_{i}^{r_0} \mathbb{Z}/p^{e_i +1}\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\emph{[Theorem~\ref{prop 4.8} and Corollary~\ref{3-4 strong}]}
Let $s = \{i \ : e_i = e_1\}$.
Write $\operatorname{exp}(\cdot)$ to denote the exponent of a group.
If $\operatorname{rk}_p A_1 < \operatorname{rk}_p A_0 +s(p-1)$ then $\operatorname{exp}(A_1)> \operatorname{exp}(A_0)$.
In particular, suppose that $s=\operatorname{rk}_p A_0 = r_0$ (in other words, suppose that $A_0 \simeq (\mathbb{Z}/p^a\mathbb{Z})^{r_0}$ and $\operatorname{exp}(A_1)= \operatorname{exp}(A_0) =p^a$).
Then $\operatorname{rk}_p A_1 =p r_0$.

body_md: With notation as before, $\operatorname{exp}(A_0) = \operatorname{exp}(A_1)=p$ if and only if $\operatorname{rk}_p(A_1)=p\cdot \operatorname{rk}_p(A_0)$.

label: ThmC
title: Heuristic
body_md:
\label{ThmC}
Fix an odd prime $p$.
Let $k_0$ denote an imaginary quadratic field and $k_1$ to denote the first layer of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension of $k_0$.
Then
\[
\Pr(\operatorname{rk}_p A_1 = d \mid \operatorname{rk}_p A_0=1) = \begin{cases}
    \frac{p-1}{p^d} & \text{ if } 1\leq d \leq p-1 \\
    \frac{1}{p^{p-1}} & \text{ if } d= p\\
    0 & \text{ if } d>p.
\end{cases}.
\]

label: genusfor
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{genusfor}
Let $K/F$ be a cyclic extension of number fields with Galois group $G$.
Let $\operatorname{Cl}(K)^{G}$ be the subgroup of $\operatorname{Cl}(K)$ consisting of the ideal classes that are fixed by the action of $G$ on $\operatorname{Cl}(K)$.
Let $\mathsf{N}_{K/F}$ denote the norm map from $K$ to $F$.
Let $E(F)$ be the unit group of $F$.
Then
\[
\#\operatorname{Cl}(K)^{G} =  \dfrac{\#\operatorname{Cl}(F)\prod_{v}e_v}{[K:F]\cdot\left[ E(F):E(F)\cap \mathsf{N}_{K/F}(K^{\times}) \right]}.
\]
where $v$ runs over all primes of $F$ and $e_v$ is the ramification index of $v$ of $F$ in $K$.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k$ be an imaginary quadratic field, and let $L/k$ be a cyclic extension of degree $p$ that is ramified at exactly one prime of $k$.
Then 
$\#\operatorname{Cl}(L)^G = \#\operatorname{Cl}(k)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $k\ne\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$.
Since $-1=\mathsf{N}_{L/k}(-1)$ and  $\pm i=\mathsf{N}_{L/k}(i)$, we have
\[
\left[ E(k):E(k)\cap \mathsf{N}_{L/k}(L^{\times}) \right]=1.
\]
When $k=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$,  the right side of Chevalley's formula is
$1/[ E(k):E(k)\cap \mathsf{N}_{L/k}(L^{\times})]$, so the index is again equal to 1.
The result follows easily.

title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We know that
\[
\# A_1^{\langle \sigma \rangle} = \# A_0.
\]
Since $\#j(A_0)=\#A_0$ and $j(A_0)$ is contained in $A_1^{\langle \sigma \rangle}$, part (a) follows.

The exact sequence $0\to A_1^{\langle \sigma \rangle} \to A_1 \to (\sigma -1)A_1\to 0$ and part (a) tell us that 
\[
\#A_0= \# A_1^{\langle \sigma \rangle} = \# A_1/(\sigma -1)A_1.
\]
Since $(\sigma-1)A_1\subseteq \ker\mathcal{N}$ and $A_1/\ker\mathcal{N}\simeq A_0$, we must have $\ker(\mathcal{N})=(\sigma-1)A_1$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{3-1}
With notation introduced in Section~\ref{sec: setup},
\[
\#A_1 \geq p^{r_0} \cdot \#A_0.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We know that $j: A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1$ is injective and $\mathcal{N}: A_1 \to A_0$ is surjective.
We also know that $\mathcal{N} \circ j = p$,
so the kernel of $\mathcal{N}$ contains $j(A_0[p])$.
In particular, $\#\ker(\mathcal{N})\geq p^{r_0}$ where $r_0$ is the $p$-rank of $A_0$.
We have
\[
\frac{\# A_1}{\# A_0} = \# \ker(\mathcal{N}) \geq p^{r_0}. \qedhere
\]
head: environment

label: thm 1 LCW write-up
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm 1 LCW write-up}
With notation introduced in Section~\ref{sec: setup},
\[
r_0 +(p-1)\operatorname{rk}_p(\overline{j}(\overline{A}_0)) \le r_1  \le p\cdot  r_0.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We deduce from Proposition~\ref{Ker N = A1^{sigma -1}} that
\[
\frac{A_1}{(\sigma -1)A_1} \simeq A_0.
\]
Let $M=A_1/(\sigma-1)A_1$.
We further have
\[
\frac{\overline{A}_1}{(\sigma-1)\overline{A}_1} \simeq \frac{A_1}{pA_1+(\sigma-1)A_1}\simeq \frac{M}{pM}\simeq \overline{A}_0.
\]
Therefore, $\operatorname{rk}_p (\overline{A}_1/(\sigma-1)\overline{A}_1) = \operatorname{rk}_p A_0 =r_0$.

Since $\sigma^p =1$, it is clear that $T^p = 0$ on $\overline{A}_1$ where $T = \sigma-1$.
In particular, $T$ is nilpotent and we can write $\overline{A}_1$ as a finite module over $\mathbb{F}_p[\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}] \simeq \mathbb{F}_p[T]/\langle T^p \rangle$, hence over $\mathbb{F}_p[T]$.
Therefore, the structure theorem for modules over a PID tells us that
\begin{equation}
\label{modp}
\overline{A}_1 \simeq \bigoplus_{i=1}^{r_0} \frac{\mathbb F_p[T]}{\langle T^{n_i}\rangle},
\end{equation}
for some integers $n_i$ with $1\le n_i\le p$.
There are $r_0$ summands because $\overline{A}_1/T\overline{A}_1$ has $p$-rank $r_0$.
This immediately yields the inequality 
\begin{equation}
\label{R as sum of ni}
r_1 = \dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} (\overline{A}_1) = \operatorname{rk}_p A_1 = \sum_{i=1}^{r_0} n_i \leq pr_0.
\end{equation}


Set $\mathsf{N} = 1 + \sigma + \ldots + \sigma^{p-1}$.
The map 
\[
\overline{A}_1 \longrightarrow \frac{\overline{A}_1}{(\sigma-1)\overline{A}_1} \longrightarrow \overline{A}_0 \longrightarrow \overline{j}(\overline{A}_0)\subseteq \overline{A}_1
\]
is the map from $\overline{A}_1$ to $\overline{A}_1$ given by 
\[
1+\sigma+\sigma^2+\cdots+\sigma^{p-1}= \sum_{i=1}^{p} \binom{p}{i}T^{i-1}\equiv T^{p-1} \pmod p.
\]
In other words, $T^p=T \overline{\mathsf{N}} = 0$ on $\overline{A}$ and $\overline{\mathsf{N}} = T^{p-1}$ on $\overline{A}$.
On a Jordan block of the form $V_n = \mathbb{F}_p[T]/\langle T^n \rangle$, the operator $T^{p-1}$ has one-dimensional image if $n=p$ and is zero otherwise.
Since $\mathsf{N}(A_1) = j(A_0)$, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{13}
\operatorname{rk}_p(\overline{j}(\overline{A}_0))=\operatorname{rk}_p( \operatorname{image}(T^{p-1}))=\#\{i \, | \, n_i=p\}.
\end{equation}
Set 
\[
c = \# \{i \mid n_i =p\}.
\]
Exactly $c$ of the Jordan blocks have length $p$, while each of the remaining $r_0-c$ blocks has length $\geq 1$, so 
\[
r_1=\sum_{i=1}^{r_0} n_i \ge cp + (r_0 - c) = r_0 + (p-1)c
\]
This completes the proof.

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{propn 4.7}
If $r_1<r_0 + p-1$ then
\[
j(A_0) \subseteq pA_1.
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
The theorem implies that $\overline{j}(\overline{A}_0)=0$.
This is equivalent to $j(A_0) \subseteq pA_1$.

label: Cor 2 from LCW write up
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since 
\[
pA_1\simeq \mathbb Z/p^{f_1-1}\mathbb Z\oplus \mathbb Z/p^{f_2-1}\mathbb Z\oplus \cdots \oplus \mathbb Z/p^{f_{r_1-1}}\mathbb Z
\]
contains $j(A_0)\simeq A_0$ as a subgroup, the result follows.

title: Remark
head: environment

label: prop 4.8
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{prop 4.8}
Let $\operatorname{exp}(A_0) = p^a$ and $s:=\#\{j: e_j = a\}$.
If $\operatorname{exp} A_1 = \operatorname{exp} A_0$, then
\[
r_1 \geq  r_0 + s(p-1).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $e_1 \geq e_2 \geq \ldots \geq e_{r_0} \geq 1$, 
\[
o(h_1) = \cdots = o(h_s) = p^a,
\]
where $h_i$ are generators of $A_0$ with order $o(h_i) = p^{e_i}$.

\noindent \textit{Claim:} The elements $\overline{j}(h_i)$, for $1\leq i \leq s$, are linearly independent in $\overline{A_1}$.

\noindent \textit{Justification:}
If not, then there exist $s$ integers $\mu_i$, not all zero mod $p$,  such that 
\[
\mu_1 j(h_1) + \cdots + \mu_s j(h_s) \in pA_1.
\]
Let
\[
x = \mu_1 h_1 + \cdots + \mu_s h_s \in A_0.
\]
Moreover $o(x) = p^a$ since some $\mu_i\not\equiv 0$ mod $p$.
Since $j(x)\in pA_1$, there exists an element $y\in A_1$ such that $j(x)=py$.
By the injectivity of $j$, we know that 
\[
o(j(x)) = o(py) = p^a.
\]
But this would mean that $y\in A_1$ has order $p^{a+1}$.
This contradicts the assumption that $\operatorname{exp}(A_1)=p^a$.
This completes the justification.

It is straightforward to conclude from \eqref{13} that
$c\geq s$.
The result follows from Theorem~\ref{thm 1 LCW write-up}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
{\it Here is an alternative proof:  $A_0$ contains a summand $S=\left(\mathbb Z/p^a\mathbb Z\right)^s$, which injects into $A_1$, both of which have exponent $p^a$.
Every cyclic subgroup of $j(S)$ of order $p^a$ is generated by an element of maximal order in $A_1$ and hence splits off as a direct summand; see \cite[Lemma~13.1.9]{judson2020abstract}.
Applying this result $s$ times shows that $j(S)$ is a direct summand of $A_1$.
Therefore, $\overline{j}(S/pS)$ is a direct summand of $\overline{A}_1$ that is contained in $\overline{j}(\overline{A}_0)$.
Therefore, $s=\operatorname{rk}_p(S/pS)\le \operatorname{rk}_p(\overline{j}(\overline{A}_0))$.
Theorem~\ref{thm 1 LCW write-up} now yields the result.}
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Theorem \ref{prop 4.8} yields a weaker version of Corollary~\ref{Cor 2 from LCW write up}: If $r_1<r_0+p-1$, then $\operatorname{exp}(A_1)>\operatorname{exp}(A_0)$.

title: Proof

For example, when $k_0=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3001057})$, we have $A_0\simeq \mathbb{Z}/9\mathbb{Z}$ and $A_1\simeq \mathbb{Z}/27\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$.}
head: environment

label: p elem
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
($\Rightarrow$)
This is Corollary~\ref{3-4 strong} with $a=1$.

($\Leftarrow$)
We know from \eqref{R as sum of ni} that 
\[
r_1 = \sum_{i=1}^{r_0} {n_i} = r_0p;
\]
thus each $n_i =p$.
We have observed previously that  $\overline{\mathsf{N}} = T^{p-1}$ on $\overline{A}_1$.
On each Jordan block $\mathbb{F}_p[T]/\langle T^p \rangle$, the image of $T^{p-1}$ is one-dimensional.
By \eqref{13} we know that $c=r_0$.
Thus $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} \overline{j}(\overline{A}_0) = r_0$.
Consider the natural surjective map
\[
(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^{r_0}  \simeq j(A_0) \longrightarrow \overline{j}(\overline{A}_0).
\]
By dimension counting, the map must be an isomorphism.
Thus the kernel is $j(A_0) \cap pA_1 =0$.

\textit{Claim: $pA_1$ is trivial, i.e., $A_1$ is an elementary $p$-group.}

\textit{Justification:}
Suppose that $pA_1$ is non-trivial.
Since multiplication by $p$ commutes with the $\sigma$ action, we know that $pA_1$ is stable under $\operatorname{Gal}(k_1/k_0) = \langle \sigma \rangle$; i.e., $\sigma(pA_1) = pA_1$.
Recall that (by orbit counting) when a $p$-group acts on a non-zero finite $p$-group, there is a non-trivial fixed point.
By definitions and Proposition~\ref{Ker N = A1^{sigma -1}} we know 
\[
(pA_1)^{\langle \sigma \rangle} = pA_1 \cap A_1^{\langle \sigma\rangle} = pA_1 \cap j(A_0) = 0,
\]
which is impossible.
This forces $pA_1$ to be trivial, as claimed.

title: Remark

label: prop growth cyclic factors
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop growth cyclic factors}
Let $G, H$ be finite abelian $p$-groups with $H\subseteq G$.
Write
\[
H\simeq \bigoplus_{i=1}^r \mathbb Z/p^{e_i}\mathbb Z, \qquad G\simeq\bigoplus_{i=1}^s \mathbb Z/p^{f_i}\mathbb Z,
\]
with $e_1\ge e_2 \ge \dots$ and $f_1\ge f_2\ge \dots$.
Let $\overline{H}=H/pH$ and $\overline{G}=G/pG$, and let $\overline{j}: \overline{H}\to \overline{G}$.
Then 
\[
\operatorname{rk}_p (\operatorname{image}(\overline{j})) \ge \#\{ i\,\mid\, e_i=f_i\}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $B=pG\cap H$.
Then $H/B\simeq (H+pG)/pG\simeq \operatorname{image}(\overline{j})$, so $|H|/|B|=p^c$, where $c=\operatorname{rk}_p( \operatorname{image}(\overline{j}))$.

Since $pH\subseteq B\subseteq H$,  
\[
B\simeq \bigoplus_{i=1}^r \mathbb Z/p^{e_i-\delta_i}\mathbb Z,
\]
with $0\le \delta_i\le 1$ for each $i$ and $\sum_i \delta_i=c$.
Moreover, $B\subseteq pG$, so $e_i-\delta_i \le  f_i-1$ for all $i$.
Because $e_i\le f_i$ for all $i$, we have
\[
c=\#\{i\,\mid\, \delta_i=1\} \ge \#\{i\,\mid\, e_i=f_i\}. \qedhere
\]
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
With the notation introduced in Section~\ref{sec: setup}, 
\[
\#\{ i\,\mid\, 1\le i\le r_0, e_i=f_i\} \le \frac{r_1-r_0}{p-1}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Theorem~\ref{thm 1 LCW write-up} implies that $\operatorname{rk}_p(\overline{j}(\overline{A}_0)) \le (r_1-r_0)/(p-1)$.
The result follows from Proposition~\ref{prop growth cyclic factors}.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
With the notation introduced in Section~\ref{sec: setup},
\[
\operatorname{rk}_p(A_1/j(A_0)) \ge r_1-c \ge \frac{(p-2)r_1+r_0}{p-1}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $e_i=0$ for $r_0< i\le r_1$.
Then 
\[
\operatorname{rk}_p(A_1/j(A_0)) \ge \#\{i\,\mid\, 1\le i\le r_1, f_i\ne e_i\}\ge r_1 - \frac{r_1-r_0}{p-1} = \frac{(p-2)r_1+r_0}{p-1}. \qedhere
\]
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: With notation as above, $\#A_1 \geq p^{r_1-c} \cdot \#A_0$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm 4.7}
Keep the notation introduced in Section~\ref{sec: setup}.
Suppose that $r_1 = r_0 =r$.

label: Prop 1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Prop 1}
Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $A$ be a finite abelian $p$-group.
Let $\sigma$ be an automorphism of $A$ with $\sigma^p =1$ and such that $\sigma=1$ on $A[p]$.
Then there exists an endomorphism $\psi$ of $A$ such that
\[
\sigma = 1+p \psi.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $A\simeq \bigoplus_{i=1}^r \mathbb{Z}/p^{g_i}\mathbb{Z}$ with $g _1 \geq \cdots \geq g_r\ge 1$.
Let
$x_i = (0, \ldots, 0, \overline{1}, 0, \ldots 0)^{\top}$ denote a generator of $A$ and note that $o(x_i) = p^{g_i}$.
Let $M=(m_{ij})$ denote the matrix corresponding to $\sigma -1$.
Then
\[
M(x_j) = \sum_{i=1}^r m_{ij}x_i
\]
We want to prove that every $m_{ij}$ is divisible by $p$, and that after dividing the matrix $M$ by $p$, we still get an endomorphism of $A$.

It is clear that $p^{g_j-1}x_j$ has order $p$ for each $j$.
Since $\sigma=1$ on $A[p]$, we observe that
\[
M(p^{g_j -1} x_j)= \sum_{i=1}^r p^{g_j-1} m_{ij}x_i =  0.
\] 
In particular, for each $i,j$ we must have that $p^{g_j-1} m_{ij}x_i=0$.
Since $o(x_i) = p^{g_i}$, it follows that $p^{g_i}\mid p^{g_j-1} m_{ij}$.
From this we can conclude that the $p$-adic valuation of $m_{ij}$ is as follows 
\begin{equation}
\label{1}
\nu_p(m_{ij})\geq \max\{0, g_i - g_j +1\}.
\end{equation}
In particular, the following three situations can arise:
\begin{equation}
\label{2}
\begin{cases}
\nu_p(m_{ij})\geq g_i - g_j +1 \geq 2 & \text{ if } g_i > g_j \\
p\mid m_{ij} & \text{ if } g_i = g_j \\
p\nmid m_{ij} & \text{ then } g_i < g_j.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
\textit{Notice the direction of implication in the third case.}

Consider a pair $(i,j)$ such that $p\nmid m_{ij}$.
Then we know from \eqref{2} that $g_i < g_j$.
Suppose we choose $(i,j)$ to be such that the difference $d=g_j - g_i>0$ is minimal.

\noindent \textit{Claim:} For $2\leq k \leq p-1$, the following congruence condition holds
\[
(M^k)_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod{p}.
\]

\noindent \textit{Justification:}
We write
\[
(M^k)_{ij} = \sum_{i_1, \ldots, i_{k-1}} m_{i i_{k-1}} m_{i_{k-1} i_{k-2}} \ldots m_{i_1 j}.
\]
(For the sake of consistency, we may write $i_k =i$ and $i_0=j$, when required.)
So a typical summand is 
\[
m_{i i_{k-1}} m_{i_{k-1} i_{k-2}} \ldots m_{i_1 j}.
\]
If this summand is not divisible by $p$, then each factor is not divisible by $p$.
In view of \eqref{2}, we have the following decreasing sequence of exponents
\[
g_j > g_{i_1} > \ldots > g_{i_{k-1}} > g_i.
\]
We assumed that $d=g_j - g_i$ is minimal; thus, such a decreasing sequence cannot exist.
Thus, each summand is divisible by $p$ and hence $(M^k)_{ij}$ is divisible by $p$.
This justifies the claim.

Next, we show that 
\begin{equation}
\label{3}
M^p \equiv 0 \pmod{p^2}.
\end{equation}
Therefore, $M^p\equiv 0 \pmod p$.
As before, we consider a summand
\[
S = m_{i_p i_{p-1}} m_{i_{p-1} i_{p-2}} \ldots m_{i_1 i_0}.
\]
Suppose that $p^2 \nmid S$.
Then $\nu_p(S)\leq 1$.
At most one factor arising in $S$ can be divisible by $p$.
Equivalently, at least $p-1$ of the other factors have $p$-valuation equal to $0$.
We know from \eqref{2} that every factor which is not divisible by $p$ forces the exponent to drop,
whereas a factor of $p$-valuation $1$ means that the exponent cannot increase.
Since $p\geq 3$, we get a contradiction since $g_j - g_i =d$ is minimal.

By assumption
\begin{equation}
\label{4}
(1+M)^p - 1 = pM + {p\choose 2}M^2 + \ldots + {p \choose p-1}M^{p-1} + M^p =0.
\end{equation}
For our choice of $(i,j)$, when $2\leq k \leq p-1$, we observe that
\[
p^2 \mid {p \choose k} (M^k)_{ij}.
\]
In addition, we also know that $p^2 \mid (M^p)_{ij}$.
By comparing with \eqref{4}, we conclude that $p\mid m_{ij}$.
This contradicts our choice of $(i,j)$.
In particular, for each pair $(i,j)$, we have shown that $p \mid m_{ij}$.

When $g_i > g_j$, the $(i,j)$-entry of $M$ has $p$-valuation $\geq g_i - g_j +1$.
Thus, $p^{g_i - g_j} \mid (m_{ij}/p)$.
On the other hand, when $g_i \leq g_j$, we have shown that $p\mid m_{ij}$.
Thus, the matrix $B=(m_{ij}/p)$ represents an endomorphism $\psi$ of $A$.
Indeed, an integer matrix $B=(b_{ij})$ represents an endomorphism of $A$ precisely when 
\[
p^{g_i - g_j}\mid b_{ij} \text{ for } g_i > g_j,
\]
(see \cite{hillar2007automorphisms}).
This follows from the fact that a homomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/p^{g_j}\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/p^{g_i}\mathbb{Z}$ sends $1 \mapsto b_{ij}$ and is well-defined precisely when $p^{g_i} \mid p^{g_j}b_{ij}$.

But $p\psi$ is nilpotent on $A_1$; hence $\sigma = 1+p\psi$ is invertible and is therefore an automorphism.
head: environment

label: Prop 2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Prop 2}
Keep the notation and assumptions in Proposition~\ref{Prop 1}.
Let $\mathsf{N} = 1 + \sigma + \sigma^2 + \ldots + \sigma^{p-1}$.
Then the kernel of $\mathsf{N}$ is $A[p]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We start by writing
\[
\mathsf{N} = 1 + \sigma + \sigma^2 + \ldots + \sigma^{p-1} = \sum_{t=0}^{p-1} (1+p\psi)^t.
\]
Since $(1+p\psi)^t \equiv 1+tp\psi \pmod{p^2}$ for all $t$, it follows immediately that
\[
\mathsf{N} \equiv p + p\psi \sum_{t=0}^{p-1} t \equiv p + p\psi \left( \frac{p(p-1)}{2}\right) \equiv p \pmod{p^2}.
\]
Equivalently, we write $\mathsf{N} = p(1+p\theta)$ where $\theta$ is an endomorphism of $A$.
But, the matrix corresponding to $1+p\theta$ has determinant $1\pmod{p}$; hence $1+p\theta$ is an automorphism.
Thus,
\[
\ker (\mathsf{N}) = \ker (p) = A[p]. \qedhere
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that $j: A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1$ is the (injective) lifting map.
Further $j(A_0) = A_1^{\langle \sigma \rangle}$.
In particular, restricting to the $p$-torsion, we have
\[
j(A_0[p]) \subseteq A_1[p]^{\langle \sigma \rangle}.
\]
Here $\sigma$ is the generator of the cyclic group $\operatorname{Gal}(k_1/k_0)\simeq \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$.
But we are assuming that the rank at the base level and the first level are equal.
In particular,
\[
\# A_0[p] = \# A_1[p] = p^r.
\]
The injectivity of $j$ now forces that
\[
j(A_0[p]) = A_1[p].
\]
Since every element of $j(A_0[p])$ is fixed by $\sigma$, it follows that every element of $A_1[p]$ is also fixed by $\sigma$.
In particular, $\sigma=1$ on $A_1[p]$.

Now, we know that the ideal norm $\mathcal{N}: A_1 \to A_0$ is surjective.
Since $\mathsf{N} = j\circ \mathcal{N}$ and $j$ is injective we know that $\ker \mathsf{N} = \ker \mathcal{N}$.
By Proposition~\ref{Prop 2} we know that the kernel is equal to $A_1[p]$.
Since 
\[
A_0 \simeq A_1/ A_1[p] \simeq \bigoplus_{i=1}^r \mathbb{Z}/p^{f_i-1}\mathbb{Z}
\]
and the cyclic factors are unique, the proof is complete.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $X={\varprojlim_n} A_n$ be the Iwasawa module of the cyclotomic $\mathbb Z_p$-extension of $k_0$.
Since $\mu (X)=0$, we know $\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb{Z}_p} X=\lambda $.
Since $X$ has no non-zero finite submodules we know that $X$ is a free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module and $X\simeq \mathbb{Z}_p^\lambda$.
Thus $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} X/pX = \lambda$.
We may view $\overline{X}$ as an $\mathbb{F}_p [T]$-module.
In particular
\[
\overline{X} \simeq \bigoplus_{i=1}^{r_0} \frac{\mathbb{F}_p [T] }{\langle T^{a_i}\rangle}.
\]
The direct sum indeed has $r_0$ components because $X/TX \simeq A_0$ and $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\overline{X}/T\overline{X}) = \operatorname{rk}_p A_0=r_0$.
We conclude that
\[
\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\overline{X}) = \lambda = \sum_{i=1}^{r_0} {a_i}.
\]
Recall that $A_n \simeq X/((1+T)^{p^n}-1)X$ and that $(1+T)^{p^n}-1\equiv T^{p^n} \pmod p$.
In the following, the first isomorphism is standard and the second is a consequence of the aforementioned structure theorem
\[
A_n/pA_n \simeq \overline{X}/T^{p^n} \overline{X} \simeq \bigoplus_{i=1}^{r_0} \frac{\mathbb{F}_p [T]}{\langle T^{\min\{a_i, p^n\}}\rangle}.
\]
Thus, we note
\[
\operatorname{rk}_{p} A_n = \sum_{i=1}^{r_0} \min \{a_i, p^n\}.
\]
We now invoke our hypothesis that $r_n<r_0 + p^n - 1$.
It is immediate that each $a_i<p^n$ and 
\[
r_n = \dim_{\mathbb{F}_p} A_n = \sum_{i} a_i =\lambda. \qedhere
\]

title: Heuristic
body_md:
\label{heuristics gen}
Fix an odd prime $p$.
Let $k_0$ denote an imaginary quadratic field with $p$ non-split and let $k_1$ be the first layer of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension of $k_0$.
Then
\[
\Pr(\operatorname{rk}_p A_1 = d \mid \operatorname{rk}_p A_0=1) = \begin{cases}
    \frac{p-1}{p^d} & \text{ if } 1\leq d \leq p-1 \\
    \frac{1}{p^{p-1}} & \text{ if } d= p\\
    0 & \text{ if } d>p.
\end{cases}
\]
